brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Two full hex base cells (piece at 0,0,0 and 1,0,0) joined side by side, with joint bolt locked and open faces capped by solid caps. check_build: meshClash clear, no errors.
Grab handle accessory (hex-acc-handle, accessory:0#0,0#3) mounted on the side of the screw cell at 0,0,0.

hex-bin-full-div2 (2-compartment bin) at 0,0,0; holds an M3 screws compartment prop and an M3 nuts compartment prop. Screws prop sits under the rim (PROP_BELOW_RIM warning was raised on it and not cleared; it is a staging prop only).
hex-bin-full-div3 (3-compartment bin) at 1,0,0; holds a 2 mm hex driver, a 5 mm hex key and a second hex driver as props.

requirements.requirement: Physical print, materials, load or safety
requirements.evidence: Configurator checks fit and collisions only; it cannot verify plastic material, strength under load, or the handle's rating. Not claimed.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell tool caddy: a full hex base at 0,0,0 with a 2-compartment bin for screws and nuts, and a full base at 1,0,0 with a 3-compartment bin for bits, a grab handle on the side of the screw cell, and capped open faces with a locked joint. The mesh check is clear. Two info-level open cap faces remain on the 0,0,0 cell, and the screws compartment prop sits below its rim. Material strength and handle load were not verified.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Trinity handle
